about.en:
The Georgetown Pre-College Summer (GPS) Program is GU-Q's flagship summer course for high school students in Qatar. For three weeks students attend full-time, co-educational, English-language classes on the Education City campus: English (critical reading, writing, presenting), Introduction to International Relations, World Geography and Global Politics, which introduces GU-Q's four majors. An optional daily SAT preparation track is taught by Princeton Review instructors, and peer tutors who are current Georgetown students run co-curricular sessions.

The programme is meant for students who want a stronger university application and a real taste of college life. The 2026 edition ran 4-23 July with an application deadline of 30 April; the 2027 edition is expected to follow the same pattern, with applications opening in spring.

It is one of the few affordable, university-run summer programmes in Doha, and it gives direct contact with GU-Q's admissions team.

Optional SAT preparation by Princeton Review
Lunch included every day

eligibility.en: Qatar nationals and residents entering the last two years of secondary school. Preference for good academic standing, a GPA of 3.0/B or 80%+ and solid English.

about.en:
Georgetown Global Challengers is GU-Q's autumn programme for students in years 10, 11 and 12. It starts with a short online classroom (Google Classroom) and continues with a week-long in-person practicum on campus. The current theme is the practical and responsible use of AI: using AI for research, writing, creativity, problem-solving and study, while learning about its limits, ethics and digital literacy.

The online part is open to anyone; students based in Qatar who complete the modules are invited to the campus bootcamp, capped at about 50 students per cohort. The 2025 edition ran online 26-30 October with campus cohorts on 2-6 and 9-13 November; the programme is offered every October-November.

Participants receive a certificate of completion. It is free and a good first contact with a Georgetown campus.

Hands-on, responsible use of AI tools
Small cohorts of about 50 students

about.en:
The University Preparedness Program is a free, asynchronous online course for high school students in grades 9-12, created by undergraduate instructors at GU-Q's Office of Educational Enrichment. It runs on Google Classroom and covers skills that matter at university, such as study habits, research and writing, and personal development.

Because it is self-paced, international students can join as easily as students in Qatar. After finishing all modules and assessments you receive a certificate of completion. The 2025 edition ran 28 September-27 November; places are first come, first served and registration closes once the class is full.

It is a no-cost way to add a Georgetown-issued certificate to your profile and practise university-style work.

about.en:
Build for QSTP is a recurring hackathon series hosted at Qatar Science & Technology Park in Education City. Each edition has its own theme and challenge brief (incubation, operations, internships, Stars of Science, sustainability, social impact and more), and teams of 2-4 developers, designers and business thinkers research, prototype and pitch within one or two days, with mentors on hand throughout.

Recent editions included the Incubation Hackathon (2-3 May 2026), Operations Hackathon (23-24 May 2026), Stars of Science Hackathon (11-14 June 2026) and an Internship Edition (30 July-2 August 2026) with cash prizes. Winning solutions can be piloted inside QSTP and first-place teams have been fast-tracked into QSTP's Entry Track.

It suits university students who want hands-on building experience and a route into Qatar's startup ecosystem. Upcoming themes are announced on the programme page and QSTP's social media.

Creative Labs is an intensive two-week studio programme at Qatar Science & Technology Park developed with NuVuX Studios. Participants join one of four parallel studios of 10-15 people (past studios: Health Wearables Devices, Games for Good, Aging in the City and more) and learn design-first principles, digital tools, 3D printing, laser cutting and prototyping by building a real project.

It is aimed at STEM educators and at school, undergraduate and graduate students interested in educational innovation and technology. The 2025 edition ran 10-21 August for 40-50 participants; QSTP currently collects registrations of interest for the next edition.

It is a rare chance in Doha to work MIT-style in a maker studio and leave with a finished prototype.

about.en:
Stars of Science is QF's flagship innovation platform, produced by Qatar Science & Technology Park. Selected innovators develop their idea into a prototype and venture with engineering, design and business mentoring, competing in a televised series watched across the Arab world. From season 18 the format puts more weight on venture-building, AI and emerging technologies.

Applications are open to entrepreneurs, engineers, scientists, designers and creators aged 18-35 from across the Arab world and the global Arab diaspora, working in fields such as AI, gaming, robotics, climate, health-tech, fashion-tech and engineering. Season 18 applications ran from 9 to 26 June 2026; the next call is expected in a similar window in 2027.

The winner receives a supported venture-building experience in Qatar: mentorship, office space, operational support and access to interns.

about.en:
My Career – My Future is QCDC's flagship job-shadowing programme, run with the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, the Ministry of Labour, the Ministry of Sports and Youth and the Civil Service and Government Development Bureau. Day 1 is an orientation at Multaqa, Education City; on days 2-4 students shadow professionals at a host organisation in their chosen field (medicine, aviation, energy, media, telecoms, finance, engineering, technology, judiciary, sport management, humanitarian work and more); day 5 is a closing ceremony with a university fair, competitions and certificates.

The 2026 edition was the largest so far and ran in early August, with registration closing in late July. QCDC also ran a Winter Edition in December 2025. The 2027 summer edition is expected to open for registration around June-July 2027.

It is the most structured way for a Qatar high school student to test a career before choosing a university major.

Over three days, organisations from government, energy, health, finance, media, security and other sectors run interactive stands and activities so students can experience different professions and understand the routes into them.

It is designed for secondary school students in Qatar's public and private schools (separate days for boys' and girls' public schools, other days for private schools and the public), as well as counsellors and parents. The seventh edition ran 28-30 September 2026 at KidZania Doha, Aspire Park; the next edition is expected in autumn 2027.

Attendance is free and usually arranged through schools.

Hands-on career activities at KidZania

about.en:
The Youth Initiatives Incubator is a strategic platform of the Ministry of Sports and Youth to discover and support youth initiatives with social and development impact and turn them from ideas into sustainable, scalable projects aligned with Qatar's National Youth Policy. Accepted initiatives go through four stages: selection, capacity-building (initiative design, strategic planning, team management, impact measurement), incubation with mentoring, technical and logistical support and partner links, and graduation.

It targets young people aged 14-35, non-profit youth teams, emerging community initiatives and young social leaders. Focus areas include social issues, youth health, environment, learning, research and innovation, employment and entrepreneurship, humanitarian work and digital media. Applications are made through the online form on the Ministry's page, with an initiative profile, operating plan and proposed budget.

about.en:
The Young Inventors Programme was launched by the Ministry of Sports and Youth at Web Summit Qatar 2026 and is run by the Qatar Scientific Club (QSC). Participants learn design thinking, engineering design and project execution, then work in teams through problem definition, idea generation, prototype design, testing and improvement, using QSC's labs and mentors.

The first cohort (35 young men and women) built seven prototypes, including a drone-detection device, a worker-safety monitoring system and a smart cast. The second cohort started on 13 September 2026 after remote interviews with applicants; new cohorts are announced on QSC's website and social media.

It suits young people who already have an invention idea and want hands-on engineering support in Arabic.

The 2026 edition, 'Pioneers of Science and Technology', ran from 28 June to 20 August and included the fifth Future Engineer programme with the Public Works Authority (Ashghal), where 40 participants developed six projects (energy saving, worker protection, pothole detection, smart cities), and the second STEM summer programme with the Qatar Society of Engineers, a two-week course ending in projects such as solar villages and sea robots.

Over five days, students move from data basics and sources to processing and quality checks, learn about Qatar's National Data Programme, and design interactive dashboards with Power BI and AI tools. The second edition ran 8-12 August 2026 with about 40 students aged 14-17. A third edition is expected in summer 2027; announcements come through QSC and NPC channels.

The National Science Promotion Program (NSPP), launched by the QU Young Scientists Center with the Office of the Vice President for Research and Graduate Studies, uses a 'learning by doing' approach. QU faculty submit STEM project proposals; each selected project hosts one QU undergraduate and two national high school students, who learn to form hypotheses, collect data, experiment and draw conclusions with professional lab equipment.

Students spend 2-4 hours a week for six months, finish with oral/poster presentations and contests, and receive certificates, volunteering letters and awards, plus opportunities to join national and international competitions. Recent projects range from functional foods for children with diabetes to materials science.
